reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space E with its Borel structure and canonical Lebesgue volume, let d=dim_R E, with no assumption d>0. For every U:E->R and nonnegative real alpha,beta, assume 0<alpha, alpha<=beta, U is globally C2, and alpha||v||^2<=D2U(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for all x,v. Put Z=integral exp(-U) against volume, a real Bochner integral with value zero if not integrable. Define mu=volume.withDensity(x -> ENNReal.ofReal(exp(-U(x))/Z)), with real division by zero equal to zero and ofReal truncating negative values to zero. This is precisely the given tilted measure. For the full standard orthonormal basis e_i indexed by Fin(d), set H(x)=sum_i D2U(x)[e_i,e_i]. Then five conclusions hold under the same mu: mu is probability; x->||grad U(x)||^2 is Bochner integrable; H is Bochner integrable; integral ||grad U||^2 dmu=integral H dmu; and this integral<=beta*d. All derivatives and gradients are actual. The numeric upper bound explicitly depends only on beta,d; alpha remains a strictly positive assumption parameter. Dimension zero uses the empty basis sum.
